title: Eye ultrasound
what: The doctor looks at the inside of the eye and the eye socket with ultrasound, through your closed eyelid.
why: When the doctor cannot see the back of the eye, for example with a cloudy lens or bleeding inside the eye, and for injuries, a suspected detached retina, or growths in the eye.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: If you had eye surgery or an eye injury
If you have a fresh wound to the eye
If your eye hurts badly or your vision dropped suddenly

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Eyes
prepare.text: Take out contact lenses. It is better to come without eye makeup.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: If your pupils will be widened with drops, it is better not to drive afterward. Check with the clinic.

steps: You sit or lie down with your eyes closed
Gel is put on your eyelid
The probe is placed gently on your closed eyelid
The doctor asks you to look up, down, right, and left
feel: Cool gel and a light touch
The gel may sting a little if it gets into your eye. It will be rinsed out
after: You can go back to your day right away
The report is usually ready right away. Your eye doctor decides the next steps
red_flags: Sudden flashes, many new floaters, or a shadow in your vision: see an eye doctor right away
A sudden drop in vision or severe eye pain: see a doctor urgently or call emergency services

faq.a: No. The probe touches the eyelid gently, and ultrasound is safe for the eye.

faq.q: Do I need to open my eye during the scan?
faq.a: No. It is done through your closed eyelid. You just move your eyes when the doctor asks.

reminders.text: Eye ultrasound tomorrow. Take out your contact lenses before the scan, and come without eye makeup.
